facts.raw_span: progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over the preceding 5 days
no prior medical history
alert (GCS 15), afebrile, and appeared well
both external ear canals were obstructed by effusion and cerumen
routine blood tests were unremarkable
Three-month history of “ear problems”
initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation
bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal
adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening
Brainstem evoked response audiometry demonstrated a threshold of 40 dB with normal wave latencies on the left
80 dB threshold with prolonged wave I latency on the right, indicating profound right-sided hearing loss
no nystagmus

concepts.why: The presence of bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal, along with adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening, and profound right-sided hearing loss, are consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The history of ear problems, including otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation, and the presence of bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, suggest the possibility of a cholesteatoma.

The presence of profound right-sided hearing loss, as demonstrated by brainstem evoked response audiometry, could be consistent with otosclerosis, although the lack of other typical findings such as conductive hearing loss and abnormal tympanometry makes this diagnosis less likely.

The history of ear problems and the presence of bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids suggest the possibility of mastoiditis, although the lack of other typical findings such as fever and otalgia makes this diagnosis less likely.
The presence of bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and adenoid hypertrophy could be consistent with eosinophilic granuloma, a type of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
